121,000 stars. An entire AI-powered trading firm, open-sourced for anyone to explore.

Analysts. Researchers. Traders. Risk managers. Portfolio managers.

«4 analyst agents covering fundamentals, sentiment, news, and technicals.

Bull and bear agents that debate every potential trade before a decision is made.

A trader agent that determines when to enter and how much to allocate.

A 3-agent risk team with aggressive, neutral, and conservative strategies.

A portfolio manager that reviews, approves, or rejects every order.

Support for Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and local models.

Built-in backtesting to evaluate strategies against historical data.»

Want to turn it into your own AI trading system? Here's the workflow:

1. Clone the repository and open it in Claude Code.

2. Ask Opus 5.5 to explain every agent in plain English so you understand how decisions are made.

3. Choose your models and configure your API keys. Use stronger models for critical decisions and cheaper ones for less demanding tasks.

4. Start with one ticker you understand. Read the full bull-versus-bear debate before trusting any output.

5. Run the built-in backtest over the last 3 years, including realistic fees and slippage. If it can't outperform buy-and-hold after costs, investigate before going further.

6. Explore broker integration, such as Alpaca for stocks or Binance for crypto.

7. Add strict safeguards: fixed position sizing, stop-loss rules, daily loss limits, and an emergency kill switch.

8. Run it in paper-trading mode for at least two weeks. Compare its performance with the backtest.

9. Connect Telegram for decision alerts. Only consider live trading after thorough testing, starting with an amount you can afford to lose.

One important reminder: an impressive AI trading architecture doesn't guarantee profitable trades. Test every strategy and never hand over your capital blindly.

Posted by Bill Sullivan | November 9, 2026 2:18 pm | Schools, Community News

From Folsom robotics lab to published author: Teen publishes teaching tool

> Folsom teen Ayushmaan Bellum transforms years of robot CAD designs into an illustrated guide to help young builders learn robotics and engineering. [...] Bellum has taught programming to more than 400 students and mentored younger robotics teams. His health technology project, Dermalytix, earned him recognition as a 2026 Conrad Innovator. His team also took third place in the Robotics Education & Competition Foundation’s international high school CAD challenge for the Gravitrack Orb, a game piece with a weight that shifts as it rolls. With the atlas, a coach can bring one of Bellum’s robot designs to a classroom he may never visit. [...] Bellum founded Cognitaur Innovation Lab in Folsom in 2025. He serves as captain, CAD designer and programmer for its robotics team, Cognitaur 29712C. Last season, he led the team to the VEX Robotics World Championship in St. Louis after it earned the Think Award at the California Region 2 championship. On Nov. 7, Cognitaur earned Tournament Champion, Robot Skills Champion and Innovate honors, according to the team.

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."
